name: Bank reconciliation preparation
summary: Before the month is signed off, your bookkeeper holds one bank reconciliation for one account: every statement line matched to the books or explained, every open item aged, a proof that the two balances agree, and the entries still to make. Nothing is posted until a person approves.

sources.title: The export form of the work: stated column headers with a stop when one does not match, the footing check of each export, reference-first matching, unpaired lines kept in the proof on their own side, entries listed for approval and never posted, and questions for named roles.

sources.contribution: One account and one period per run; matching on amount, payee and a business-day date window stated on the result; one sign convention for both sides before comparing; each side's own description shown for a matched pair; no pairing where a line has more than one equally good candidate; ending balances compared instead of relying on matches; nothing changed on either side.

Matching on reference numbers as well as amount and date; a kind for every unmatched item; ageing brackets for open items; the two-sided proof with no balancing line; last period's open items carried and aged again; flags for lingering deposits and long-outstanding payments; preparer and reviewer sign-off.
